content: The test image shows a soybean stem at a node with a grayish-white, fluffy/cottony fungal growth at the junction. The surrounding leaves are yellowed. Key candidates: White_Mold (cottony mycelium on stems), Powdery_Mildew (white powdery growth), Downy_mildew (whitish fungal mass).

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Close-up of soybean stem at a node showing **grayish-white, fluffy/cottony fungal growth** at the petiole/stem junction. Surrounding leaves are yellowed (late season).

- **White_Mold reference** (top-left panel): Shows nearly identical white cottony mycelium growing on the stem at a node — exact match in texture, color, and location.

- **Powdery_Mildew**: Shows powdery coating on leaf surfaces — no stem node growth. Ruled out.

- **Downy_mildew**: Shows leaf symptoms (whitish patches on leaves) — not stem node growth. Ruled out.

The fluffy cottony mycelial mass at the stem node is the hallmark sign of Sclerotinia stem rot (White Mold). The White Mold reference images confirm this exact presentation.
